citations.quote:
Fix integers $r,n\ge1$. Put $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$ and $p(X)=\prod_{a=1}^r(X-u_a)$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the unital associative $R$-algebra on generators $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ and $X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}$, with central $R$-action, subject to

$$ (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1), $$

$$ X_jX_k=X_kX_j,\qquad T_iX_j=X_jT_i\ (j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}. $$

Here the braid relation is imposed for $1\le i<n-1$ and the distant commutation relation for $1\le i,j<n$. Define the **multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $r$ and rank $n$** by

$$ H_{r,n}=\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}/(p(X_1)), $$

where $(p(X_1))$ denotes the two-sided ideal it generates. The unit $Q$ and the quadratic relation make every $T_i$ invertible, with $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. The cyclotomic relation also gives the polynomial inverse

$$ X_1^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}(u_1\cdots u_r)^{-1}\bigl(X_1^{r-1}-e_1X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}e_{r-1}\bigr), $$

where $e_k$ is the $k$th elementary symmetric polynomial in $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. The presentation already includes inverse generators; this formula records that the quotient does not require a separate inverse parameter. For $i\ge1$, write $X_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i$ when using the recursion determined by the affine relation.

This is the multiplicative presentation. It is not the additive degenerate cyclotomic presentation obtained after setting a parameter equal to $1$ and changing generators.

In $H_{r,n}$ define

$$ L_1=X_1,\qquad L_i=Q^{1-i}T_{i-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{i-1}\quad(2\le i\le n). $$

Then $L_i=X_i$ for every $i$, so the $L_i$ commute and are units. For $1\le i<n$ they satisfy

$$ T_iL_iT_i=QL_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_i=L_{i+1}T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_{i+1}=L_iT_i+(Q-1)L_{i+1}, $$

and $T_iL_j=L_jT_i$ when $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$. More generally, for every polynomial $f\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$,

$$ T_if(L_1,\ldots,L_n)=f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{f(L_1,\ldots,L_n)-f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)}{L_i-L_{i+1}}, $$

where $s_i$ interchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st variables and the displayed divided difference is a polynomial. In particular the cyclotomic relation transports as

$$ T_ip(L_i)=p(L_{i+1})T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1})}{L_i-L_{i+1}}. $$

When $p(L_i)=0$, this gives $p(L_{i+1})T_i=(Q-1)L_{i+1}(p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1}))/(L_i-L_{i+1})$; the cyclotomic quotient guarantees this only for $i=1$. It does **not** impose $p(L_i)=0$ for every $i$.

Let $(S,m)$, $W$, $\ell$ be as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]; let $R$, $v_s$, $H$, $T_s$ be as in [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]]; let $T_w$ for $w\in W$ and the spanning statement be as in [[lem-hh-reduced-word-independence-and-length-multiplication]]; and let $E$, $P_s$, $Q_s$ and $P_w$ be as in [[lem-hh-commuting-left-right-hecke-length-operators]].

1. **The length-operator representation.** There is a unique unital $R$-algebra homomorphism $\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(E)$ with $\rho(T_s)=P_s$ for all $s\in S$; it satisfies $\rho(T_w)=P_w$ and $\rho(T_w)(e_1)=e_w$ for all $w\in W$.
2. **Standard basis.** $\{T_w:w\in W\}$ is an $R$-basis of $H$: it spans by [[lem-hh-reduced-word-independence-and-length-multiplication]] and is $R$-linearly independent. Hence $H$ is free as an $R$-module and every element of $H$ has a unique expansion $\sum_wa_wT_w$ with $a_w\in R$ and all but finitely many $a_w$ zero.
3. **Faithfulness.** $\rho$ is injective.
4. **Base change.** For every commutative ring $R'$ and every ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$, the scalar extension $R'\otimes_RH$ is, as an $R'$-algebra, canonically isomorphic to the quotient of the free associative $R'$-algebra on $(T_s)_{s\in S}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the images under $\varphi$ of the relations (Q) and (B) of [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]], and it is free as an $R'$-module with basis $(1\otimes T_w)_{w\in W}$. No flatness or freeness of $R'$ over $R$ is assumed, and no torsion-freeness or semisimplicity of $H$ or of its specialisations is claimed.

Let $n\ge2$, $R_0=\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]$, and let $H_{n,Q}^{\mathrm{fin}}$ be the unital associative $R_0$-algebra presented by generators $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$, relations $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$, and the type-$A_{n-1}$ braid relations. For $w\in S_n$, let $T_w$ be the product along a reduced expression of $w$. Then $T_w$ is well-defined and
$$
\{T_w:w\in S_n\}
$$
is an $R_0$-basis of $H_{n,Q}^{\mathrm{fin}}$. For every commutative $R_0$-algebra $R'$, the scalar extension $R'\otimes_{R_0}H_{n,Q}^{\mathrm{fin}}$ has basis $(1\otimes T_w)_{w\in S_n}$.

derivations.claim: For $n=1$, the relation $p(X_1)=0$ and its unit constant coefficient express $X_1^{-1}$ as a polynomial in $X_1$; monic division then spans the algebra by $1,X_1,\ldots,X_1^{r-1}$, as required. Hence assume $n\ge2$. If $r=1$, $X_1=u_1$, the affine recursion and $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$ express every $X_i$ and $X_i^{-1}$ in the finite generators. Thus the multiplicative finite type-A algebra over $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1}]$ maps surjectively to $H_{1,n}$, fixing each $T_i$. By [F4] and coefficient extension from $R_0$ to $R$, its basis is $(T_w)$, so the images span $H_{1,n}$; these are precisely the proposed PBW words when all exponents are $0$. For $r\ge2$ set $R'=R[v,w]/(v^2-Q,\ w^r-(-1)^{r+1}e_r)$. Successive division by these monic polynomials gives the $R$-basis $v^iw^j$ with $0\le i<2$, $0\le j<r$, containing $1$; thus $R'$ is free of positive rank. Also $v^{-1}=vQ^{-1}$ and $w^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}e_r^{-1}w^{r-1}$.

Set $a=v-v^{-1}$, $s_j=v^{-1}T_{j-1}$ for $2\le j\le n$, and $z=w^{-1}X_1$. Scaling gives $s_j^2=as_j+1$, the type-A braid relations, and $zs_j=s_jz$ only for $j\ge3$. The affine relation gives $zs_2zs_2=s_2zs_2z$: before scaling the two sides are $X_1T_1X_1T_1=QX_1X_2$ and $T_1X_1T_1X_1=QX_2X_1$. Expanding $\prod_{c=1}^r(wz-u_c)=0$ and using $w^r=(-1)^{r+1}e_r$ gives $z^r=b_1z^{r-1}+\cdots+b_{r-1}z+1$, where $b_k=(-1)^{k+1}e_kw^{-k}$. Hence powers of $z$ reduce to $0\le j<r$, and $z,s_2,\ldots,s_n$ generate the extended algebra.

Put $s=s_2$, $Y=szs$, and $\mathcal N_2=\operatorname{Span}_{R'}\{z^c,z^csz^d,z^csz^ds:0\le c,d<r\}$. The rank-four braid gives $Yz=zY$, and expansion of $Y^2=szs^2zs$ using $s^2=as+1$ gives $Y^2=a^2zY+azsz+sz^2s$, hence $sz^2s=Y^2-a^2zY-azsz$. Inductively every $Y^m$, $1\le m<r$, is in $\mathcal N_2$: multiply a term of each of the three displayed forms by $Y$, use $sY=aY+zs$, $z^dszs=szsz^d$, and $s^2=as+1$, then reduce every excess $z$ power by the monic relation. In particular $z^csz^dsY=az^{c+d}Y+z^{c+1}sz^d$, and $z^csz^dsY$ with a final $s$ first expands its middle $s^2$ into this expression and $z^csz^{d+1}s$. Also $Ys=aY+sz$ and $Yz=zY$, so induction gives $Y^ms$ as a sum of $Y^m,zY^{m-1},\ldots,z^{m-1}Y,sz^m$, all in $\mathcal N_2$.

For $U_m=sz^ms$, $1\le m<r$, induction gives $U_m\in\operatorname{Span}\{z^c,z^cs,z^cY^q,z^csz^d:c<r,\ 1\le q\le m,\ 1\le d\le m-1\}$. The base terms are $U_1=Y$ and $U_2=Y^2-a^2zY-azsz$. For $m\ge3$, inserting $s^{-1}s$ between $z^{m-1}$ and $z$ gives $U_m=U_{m-1}Y-a\,sz^{m-1}Y$, while the rank-four braid and quadratic relation give $sz^{m-1}Y=az^{m-1}Y+zsz^{m-1}$. Multiplication of the four inductive term types by $Y$ uses $z^cY$, $sY=aY+zs$, $z^cY^qY=z^cY^{q+1}$, and $z^csz^dY=az^{c+d}Y+z^{c+1}sz^d$; every resulting exponent at least $r$ is reduced by the monic polynomial. This proves the induction. It also proves $U_mz^d,U_mz^ds\in\mathcal N_2$: commute $z^d$ across $Y^q$, expand $Y^q$ and $Y^qs$ by step 1.3, and reduce excess powers. The corrected coefficient identity in the rank-two induction is $a z^c s z^{c'}s z s=a^2z^{c+c'}Y+a z^{c+1}s z^{c'}$. Left multiplication by $s$ on $z^c$, $z^csz^d$, $z^csz^ds$ gives respectively $sz^c$, $U_cz^d$, $U_cz^ds$; for $c=0$ use $s^2=as+1$. Thus $\mathcal N_2$ is stable under $z,s$, contains $1$, and equals the rank-two algebra.

For $i\ge2$ put $\Lambda_1=\{z^c:0\le c<r\}$, $D_i(j)=s_i\cdots s_j$ for $2\le j\le i$, and $D_i(i+1)=1$. Put $L_i(c)=D_i(2)z^c$ for $1\le c<r$, $L_i(0)=D_i(2)$, and $S_i(c,j)=D_i(2)z^cs_2\cdots s_j$ for $1\le c<r$, $2\le j\le i$. Let $\Lambda_i$ contain $1$, all $D_i(j)$, all $L_i(c)$ with $c>0$, and all $S_i(c,j)$. Then $|\Lambda_1|=r$, $|\Lambda_i|=ir$, and step 2.1 gives the base $M_2=H_{r,2}\otimes_RR'$ for $M_n=\operatorname{Span}_{R'}(\Lambda_1\cdots\Lambda_n)$. If $M_{n-1}=H_{r,n-1}\otimes_RR'$, the older generators preserve $M_n=M_{n-1}\Lambda_n$. Write each prefix as $h'a_{n-1}$ with $h'\in H_{r,n-2}\otimes_RR'$, $a_{n-1}\in\Lambda_{n-1}$; $s_n$ commutes with $h'$, so it remains to reduce $s_n(a_{n-1}a_n)$. For $a_n=1$, $s_nD_{n-1}(j)=D_n(j)$, $s_nL_{n-1}(c)=L_n(c)$, and $s_nS_{n-1}(c,j)=S_n(c,j)$. If $a_{n-1}=1$, use $s_nD_n(j)=aD_n(j)+D_{n-1}(j)$ and, for loops or sandwiches, $s_nD_n(2)=aD_n(2)+D_{n-1}(2)$ followed by the finite coset factorization proved next. These terms are in $H_{r,n-1}\Lambda_n$.

The finite group has the left-coset decomposition $\mathfrak S_n=\mathfrak S_{n-1}\{D_n(j):2\le j\le n+1\}$, where $D_n(n+1)=1$: the representatives place the value $n$ in distinct positions, and left multiplication by $\mathfrak S_{n-1}$ reorders the other values. Their lengths are $n-j+1$, the inversions involving $n$; inversions among the other values are exactly those of the left factor, so lengths add. By [F3], every finite Hecke word therefore expands into $H_{r,n-1}\{D_n(j)\}$. This proves the repeated-square propagation as well: $D_n(3)s_2^2s_3\cdots s_i$ is finite for $2\le i\le n$, and expanding each square by $s_m^2=as_m+1$ leaves finite words to which the same factorization applies. The braid sweep used below is $D_n(3)s_2s_3\cdots s_j=s_2s_3\cdots s_{j-1}D_n(2)$ for $2\le j\le n$: the base is $D_n(3)s_2=D_n(2)$, and $D_n(2)s_m=s_{m-1}D_n(2)$ for $3\le m\le n$, obtained by commuting the rightmost $s_m$ past $s_{m-2},\ldots,s_2$, applying the adjacent braid, then commuting $s_{m-1}$ past $s_n,\ldots,s_{m+1}$.

A last-stage word in $\Lambda_n$ contains no $X$ or one factor $z^k=w^{-k}X_1^k$ with $0\le k<r$, so its total nonnegative $X$-degree is below $r$. Repeatedly apply [F2] to move polynomial factors left of Hecke generators; the divided-difference correction preserves nonnegative exponents and total degree. Thus each last-stage word becomes a sum of $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_n^{a_n}T_y$ with $\sum a_i<r$.

The first three final-factor cases are as follows. For descending/descending, $s_nD_{n-1}(i)D_n(j)=D_{n-1}(j-1)D_n(i)$ if $i<j$, and $=aD_{n-1}(i)D_n(j)+D_{n-1}(j)D_n(i+1)$ if $i\ge j$: slide the leading $s_n$ through the overlapping descending string by the adjacent braid; at the common $s_i$ use $s_i^2=as_i+1$ to obtain the second branch. For descending/loop, $s_nD_{n-1}(i)D_n(2)z^k=aD_{n-1}(i)L_n(k)+L_{n-1}(k)D_n(i+1)$; in the second term commute $z^k$ left past $s_n,\ldots,s_3$. For descending/sandwich, $s_nD_{n-1}(i)S_n(k,j)=aD_{n-1}(i)S_n(k,j)+S_{n-1}(k,j)D_n(i+1)$ if $j<i$, and $=aD_{n-1}(i)S_n(k,j)+S_{n-1}(k,j-1)D_n(i)$ if $j\ge i$; after the quadratic term, move the remaining suffix $s_2\cdots s_j$ left past $D_n(i+1)$ when $j<i$, and past $D_n(i)$ stopping at $s_{j-1}$ when $j\ge i$. In the second branch $S_{n-1}(k,1)=L_{n-1}(k)$.

For loop/descending, $s_nL_{n-1}(k)D_n(j)=D_{n-1}(2)S_n(k,2)$ if $j=2$, and $=D_{n-1}(j-1)L_n(k)$ if $j>2$; the first is the tail $D_n(2)z^ks_2$, and the second moves $z^k$ left past $s_n,\ldots,s_3$. For loop/loop, the $j=2$ sweep leaves $D_{n-1}(2)D_n(3)(sz^ksz^l)$; step 2.1 expands the parenthesized tail into $z^c$, $z^csz^{c'}$, and $z^csz^{c'}s$ (with $c'>0$ in the last type), giving respectively $L_{n-1}(c)D_n(3)$, $L_{n-1}(c)L_n(c')$, and $L_{n-1}(c)S_n(c',2)$ because $D_n(3)s=D_n(2)$. For loop/sandwich, append $s_2\cdots s_j$ to those three tails. The first is finite after the old prefix. The second is $D_n(2)z^{c'}s_2\cdots s_j=S_n(c',j)$ when $c'>0$, and finite when $c'=0$. In the third, expand the final $s^2$: its $a$-term is the preceding sandwich, while the other term has tail $D_n(3)sz^{c'}s_3\cdots s_j$; commute $z^{c'}$ across $s_3,\ldots,s_j$ and use step 4.1 to obtain an old-algebra prefix followed by $L_n(c')$.

Factor $y=hD_n(j)$ length-additively with $h\in\mathfrak S_{n-1}$. Since $X_n$ commutes with $X_1,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ and $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-2}$, each term lies in $H_{r,n-1}X_n^{a_n}T_{D_n(j)}$, with $a_n<r$. Induction on $n$ therefore proves bounded PBW spanning over $R'$.

For sandwich/descending, $s_nS_{n-1}(k,i)D_n(j)=D_{n-1}(i+1)S_n(k,i+1)$ if $j=i+1$, $=D_{n-1}(j-1)S_n(k,i)$ if $i<j-1$, and $=D_{n-1}(j)S_n(k,i+1)$ if $i\ge j$. These are obtained by moving the descending string through the ascending suffix: at each index use $s_ms_{m-1}s_m=s_{m-1}s_ms_{m-1}$ and commute letters at distance at least two; the three stopping points are respectively after $s_{i+1}$, before the suffix, and after crossing $s_i$. For sandwich/loop, the $j=2$ sweep gives $D_{n-1}(2)D_n(3)(sz^ksz^l)s_3\cdots s_{i+1}$. Expand the rank-two tail as $z^c$, $z^csz^{c'}$, $z^csz^{c'}s$. The first is finite after an old-algebra prefix. In the second, $c'=0$ leaves a finite tail; for $c'>0$, commute $z^{c'}$ through the suffix and use $D_n(3)s_2\cdots s_{i+1}=s_2\cdots s_iD_n(2)$ to obtain an old prefix times $L_n(c')$. In the third, $D_n(3)sz^{c'}s=D_n(2)z^{c'}s$, giving the old prefix times $S_n(c',i+1)$. For sandwich/sandwich, append $s_2\cdots s_j$ to the same expansion; the three terms are $D_{n-1}(2)z^cD_n(4)s_3^2s_4\cdots s_{i+1}(s_2\cdots s_j)$, $D_{n-1}(2)z^cs_2\cdots s_iD_n(2)z^{c'}(s_2\cdots s_j)$, and $D_{n-1}(2)z^cD_n(2)z^{c'}s_2\cdots s_{i+1}(s_2\cdots s_j)$. The first is finite after an old prefix. The second is an old prefix times $S_n(c',j)$ for $c'>0$, and finite for $c'=0$. In the third, for $j\le i$ the mixed braid sweep is $D_n(2)z^{c'}s_2\cdots s_{i+1}s_2\cdots s_j=(s_2\cdots s_j)D_n(2)z^{c'}s_2\cdots s_{i+1}$; for $j>i$ it is $(s_2\cdots s_{j-1})D_n(2)z^{c'}s_2\cdots s_i$. At the $s_2$ boundary use $z^d s_2 z s_2=s_2 z s_2 z^d$: it is the rank-four relation for $d=1$, and if it holds for $d$, then $z^{d+1}s_2zs_2=z^d(zs_2zs_2)=z^d(s_2zs_2z)=(z^ds_2zs_2)z=s_2zs_2z^{d+1}$. All higher crossings use the ordinary adjacent braid. Thus $c'>0$ gives an old prefix times $S_n(c',i+1)$ or $S_n(c',i)$, and $c'=0$ leaves a finite word. All nine cases land in $H_{r,n-1}\Lambda_n$, proving that $M_n$ is stable under every generator and contains $1$.

Let $M$ be the $R$-span of the proposed PBW family and $C=H_{r,n}/M$. Right exactness identifies $R'\otimes_RC$ with the quotient of the extended algebra by that family, which is zero by step 5.3. Because $R'$ is free with basis containing $1$, $R'\otimes_RC$ contains $C$ as a direct summand; hence $C=0$.

The preceding steps prove integral spanning, including $r=1$ and faithful-free descent. The cyclotomic relation is used only on $X_1$; higher generators enter through their actual affine transport and the explicit normal-word reductions.

boundaries.reason: The definition used by the Statement assumes positive r,n.
The Statement assumes all parameters are units.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 handles n=1 for every r explicitly and uses the multiplicative basis only for n>=2.
Statement is universal over the integral Laurent ring; the repair invokes arbitrary coefficient extension and no specialized nondegeneracy.

boundaries.reason: The Statement has no interval endpoint assertion.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and proof use finite generators, explicit words, finite free bases and specified homomorphisms; no arbitrary choice is needed.

boundaries.reason: The Statement is not an if-and-only-if assertion.

is an $R_0$-basis of $H_{n,Q}^{\mathrm{fin}}$. For every commutative $R_0$-algebra $R'$, the scalar extension $R'\otimes_{R_0}H_{n,Q}^{\mathrm{fin}}$ has basis $(1\otimes T_w)_{w\in S_n}$.

derivations.claim: The recursion in the definition gives $L_1=X_1$. If $L_i=X_i$, then $L_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iL_iT_i=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i=X_{i+1}$ by [F1]. Induction proves $L_i=X_i$ for all $i$, and the commutation and unit claims follow from the affine presentation.

The equality $T_iL_iT_i=QL_{i+1}$ is [F1]. Right-multiplying it by $T_i^{-1}$ and using [F2] gives $T_iL_i=QL_{i+1}T_i^{-1}=L_{i+1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. Left-multiplying by $T_i^{-1}$ gives $L_iT_i=(T_i-(Q-1))L_{i+1}$, which is equivalent to the displayed relation for $T_iL_{i+1}$. The distant relation is [F1].

The failure of a common cyclotomic polynomial already occurs at level $r=1$, rank $n=2$. Here $X_1=u_1$ and $L_2=Q^{-1}T_1X_1T_1=u_1Q^{-1}T_1^2=u_1+(Q-1)u_1Q^{-1}T_1$. Put $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1)$ and take the multiplicative finite type-A algebra over $K$, which has basis $1,T_1$ by [F3]. Regard it as an $R$-algebra through the coefficient injection $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1}]\hookrightarrow K$. There is an algebra map from this presented quotient to that finite type-A target sending $T_1$ to its generator, $X_1$ to $u_1$, and $X_2$ to $Q^{-1}u_1T_1^2$: the affine relation holds by construction, the $X_j$ commute because $X_1$ maps to a scalar, and all inverse generators map to units. Under this map, $p(L_2)=L_2-u_1$ becomes $(Q-1)u_1Q^{-1}T_1$, which is nonzero because $T_1$ is a basis vector by [F3] and $(Q-1)u_1Q^{-1}$ is nonzero in $K$. Thus $p(L_2)$ was already nonzero in the cyclotomic quotient. The initial cyclotomic relation gives a transport identity, not the same polynomial relation on every $L_i$.

Put $\delta_i(f)=(f-s_if)/(X_i-X_{i+1})$. For a monomial $X_i^aX_{i+1}^b$ with $a,b\ge0$, the numerator is divisible by $X_i-X_{i+1}$: if $a\ge b$ it equals $X_i^bX_{i+1}^b(X_i^{a-b}-X_{i+1}^{a-b})$, and if $b>a$ interchange the two variables. Thus $\delta_i(f)$ is a polynomial for every polynomial $f$. The generator cases of step 1.2 give $T_if=s_i(f)T_i-(Q-1)X_{i+1}\delta_i(f)$ for $f=X_i,X_{i+1}$; it is immediate for every other variable and for coefficients in $R$. The identity $\delta_i(fg)=\delta_i(f)g+s_i(f)\delta_i(g)$ then extends the same formula from $f,g$ to $fg$, and linearity proves it for every polynomial. Replacing $X_j$ by $L_j$ using step 1.1 yields the stated transport rule.

Take $f(X_i)=p(X_i)$ in the general transport formula. It gives the first displayed identity for every $i$. For $i=1$, $p(L_1)=p(X_1)=0$ by definition, so the identity specializes to the stated conditional relation. The quotient by $L_i-L_{i+1}$ is a divided difference polynomial, not an inverse of that element. No cancellation of $T_i$ or of a content difference is involved.
Steps 1.1–3.1 establish the commuting generators and all claimed transport identities, including the explicit non-common-polynomial example.
